[color=#ff7700][size=6][b]Description:[/b][/size][/color]
[size=6]A pile of small QoL mods I made, merged into one. The point is being able to change whatever part of the game you want, for your own balance, roleplay, or whatever reason you have, without hunting down a separate mod for every number.

One page for every thing in the game. Search a name, open it, change its numbers. Everything starts at vanilla and nothing changes until you switch it on.

The Features tab holds the rules that belong to no single thing, plus extras covering what mods like Pick Up And Haul, Increased Stack and door mats do. My own implementations, done the way I wanted them.

On performance: a switch that is off costs nothing. Changing numbers is a read at startup and again when you close the settings window, so it costs nothing while you play. A few of the Features extras do run during play and their cost is small but not zero.

It adds one buildable thing, a door mat, so removing the mod mid-save removes any you have placed.[/size]

nodes.summary: I made this mod because another similar one didn't work for me.
nodes.description:
Steam Workshop

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3779351608][size=3]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3779351608[/size][/url][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3779351608][/url]


[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
It got annoying in RimWorld whenever I build a new shelf pawns start filling it up with unwanted things before you can set the filters for what it's supposed to be for. And in vanilla RimWorld shelves have a higher priority than floor stockpiles so they waste time moving things your want on the floor to the shelves. This mod tries to make all storage except for bookcases have "Normal" priority and have all items on the filter disabled by default.

My belief is that benches/bills/storage should start with an empty filter with all options disabled and you should choose what you want to enable, instead of the opposite where you start with every dumb thing enabled and have to individually disable many things you don't want.

nodes.name: Arabic Translation
nodes.summary: Full Arabic language translation and interface support for RimWorld.
nodes.description:
[b]RimWorld Arabic Translation[/b]

Full Arabic language support for RimWorld, covering the base game and all official DLCs.

🛠️ [b]Available Versions[/b]

To work around game engine limitations with Arabic text rendering, three distinct versions are available under the Files tab:

1. Data-ArabicSupport (Recommended)
  - Comes bundled with the required ArabicSupport mod.
  - Enables natural top-to-bottom reading order with correct word wrapping and line lengths.[color=#00ff00](With mod)[/color]

2. Data-WordWrap
  - Features connected Arabic characters and top-to-bottom reading, with text aligned to the left side.[color=#ff0000](Without mod)[/color]

3. Data-Normal
  - Features connected Arabic characters and standard line lengths, but text reads from bottom-to-top.[color=#ff0000](Without mod)[/color]

🚀 [b]Installation[/b]

1. Download your preferred package from the Files tab.
2. Extract the ZIP archive.
3. Copy the extracted folders and paste them directly into your root RimWorld game directory:
  - Steam default path:
    C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RimWorld
  - GOG default path:
    C:\GOG Games\RimWorld

(Note: If you are installing the Data-ArabicSupport version, extracting it directly to the root RimWorld directory will place both the translation files and the mod into their correct folders automatically).

💬 [color=#ffffff]Feedback and Support[/color]

If you encounter typos, missing text, or inaccurate translations, feedback is always welcome:
- Leave a comment in the Posts tab or submit a report under the Bugs tab.
- Please include the current text, your suggested replacement, and an in-game screenshot showing where the text appears.

nodes.name: No Quality For Equipment
nodes.summary: Removes quality modifiers for weapons and apparel.
nodes.description:
[size=3]Steam Workshop[/size]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3778646760][size=3]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3778646760[/size][/url]

[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]

Inspired by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3544594291]Prisoner Jumpsuits - No Quality[/url].

This mod removes quality modifiers from:
ApparelBase
BaseGunWithQuality
BaseMeleeWeapon_Sharp_Quality
BaseMeleeWeapon_Blunt_Quality
BaseWeaponNeolithic

So now weapons/apparel should no longer spawn with different quality.

Combat Extended already has its own mechanics for low HP equipment losing effectiveness. Some mods already add mechanics for repairing equipment so I found the extra random crafting/spawning quality to be unnecessary bloat. Especially since when legendary equipment goes to to 1% HP they are still legendary, when awful equipment is repaired and goes up to 100% HP they are still awful. Now only HP should effect the "quality" of equipment by indirectly modifying value and effectiveness.

nodes.summary: Autonomous Caravan Animals removes the repetitive work of manually roping animals during caravan preparation. Eligible pen animals walk to the caravan gathering point on their own, wait with the caravan, and then travel independently to the
nodes.description:
[b]Tired of colonists wasting half the day roping animals for caravans?[/b]

In vanilla RimWorld, forming a caravan with pack animals is painful:
[list]
[*]Colonists have to rope every animal to the gathering point[/*]
[*]Then rope them again to the map exit[/*]
[*]When the caravan returns, they have to drag the animals all the way back from the edge of the map to their pens[/*]
[/list]
This gets especially bad with more than a few animals. Your handlers get exhausted, mental break, or just take forever while the rest of the colony sits around waiting.

[b]Autonomous Caravan Animals fixes this.[/b]

Eligible pen animals now move themselves:
[list]
[*]Walk to the caravan gathering point on their own[/*]
[*]Walk to the map exit when the caravan is ready to leave[/*]
[*]Walk straight back to a suitable pen when the caravan returns[/*]
[/list]Colonists can focus on loading items and other caravan tasks instead of constantly chasing animals with ropes.

Works with both enclosed pens and open pen markers.

[size=6]What are "Extinct & Engineered" Birds?[/size]

A mix of genetically resurrected and gene-engineered birds. Species brought back from extinction, modified for human needs, or abandoned as failed corporate experiments.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GrHGnQs.png[/img]

[size=5]Companion Birds[/size]
[b][size=4]Kākāpo[/size][/b]
A flightless, moss-green "owl-parrot" restored from near-extinction and beloved as a therapy pet. Glitterworld gene-crafters gave it an engineered psychic gland that radiates a soothing aura to compliment its placid temperament and famously sweet aroma; its mere presence helps keep nearby colonists calm and pleasant.

[b][size=4]Kākāriki[/size][/b]
A small, brilliantly colored parakeet revived through glitterworld cloning, endlessly curious and quick to bond with humans. Its social nature means it's just as happy perched on a colonist's shoulder or poking its beak into whatever its owner happens to be doing, offering frequent nuzzles and mood boosting companionship.

[size=5]Mounts[/size]
[b][size=4]Moa[/size][/b]
Resurrected from extinction and bio-engineered into a tall, powerful, horse-sized pack animal built for cold forests and uneven tundra. Docile and sure-footed, it hauls heavy loads reliably where other mounts often struggle.

[size=4][b]Elephant Bird[/b][/size]
A colossal bio-engineered avian enhanced to grow beyond a Megasloth in stature, its dense, interlocking plumage forms natural armor that shrugs off small-arms fire. Docile until provoked - then its reinforced kicks from taloned feet and snapping beak can crack mechanoid plating or tear opponent's limbs off.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/uqo5OHp.png[/img]

[size=5]Utility Birds[/size]
[b][size=4]Great Auk[/size][/b]
A stout, cold-adapted seabird genetically resurrected and engineered for colonies on ice-world extremes where other poultry can't survive. Clumsy on land but unbothered by lethal cold, it needs little temperature management and provides insulating down and blubber-rich meat.

[b][size=4]Kiwi[/size][/b]
Saved from extinction through conservation efforts, then genetically enhanced to lay an even larger version of its already famously oversized egg. Tiny, quiet, and easily overlooked by predators, it's a low-maintenance source for absurdly sized eggs.

[b][size=4]Rodrigues Solitaire[/size][/b]
Resurrected from extinction alongside its cousin the dodo, then gene-edited to be a flock-friendly large-scale farmable poultry bird. Glitterworld epicureans prize its meat above the fattier dodo's, seeking it out specifically for its lean texture and rich flavor.

[b][size=4]Slag Snipe[/size][/b][i](a strange cousin to the utility birds)[/i]
Nobody's quite sure why this bird exists. Immune to chemical poisoning though almost useless otherwise, it feeds on corpses, refuse, and even toxic sludge - accumulating those toxins into meat that's dangerously unstable to eat, while giving colonists a case of the creeps with its looks and odors.

nodes.name: Shelf Limiter
nodes.summary: Set a separate maximum amount for every resource stored on vanilla shelves.
nodes.description:
[b][size=5]Shelf Limiter[/size][/b]

Shelf Limiter is a lightweight RimWorld 1.6 mod that lets you set a separate maximum amount for every resource stored on a vanilla shelf.
The limits are added directly beside each resource in the vanilla shelf storage menu. Leave a field empty to preserve normal vanilla behavior.

[b][size=4]Features[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Set a separate maximum for every resource.[/*]
[*]Limits apply across the entire selected shelf.[/*]
[*]Automatically caps values at each resource’s physical shelf capacity.[/*]
[*]Prevents pawns from delivering more than the selected limit.[/*]
[*]Accounts for resources that pawns are already carrying to the shelf.[/*]
[*]Lowering a limit makes only the excess amount available for hauling.[/*]
[*]Every limit persists in saved games.[/*]
[/list]
[b][size=4]Scope[/size][/b]

Shelf Limiter affects only the vanilla Shelf and Small Shelf buildings.
Stockpile zones, dumping zones, containers, and modded storage buildings are not changed.


[b][size=4]Requirements[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]RimWorld 1.6[/*]
[*][url=https://github.com/pardeike/HarmonyRimWorld/releases/latest][/url][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2009463077]Harmony[/url][/*]
[/list]Keep Harmony above Shelf Limiter in the mod load order.


[b][size=4]Installation[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Download and extract Shelf Limiter.[/*]
[*]Place the Shelf Limiter folder inside RimWorld’s Mods directory.[/*]
[*]Enable Harmony and Shelf Limiter in the mod list.[/*]
[*]Keep Harmony above Shelf Limiter in the load order.[/*]
[/list]
[b][size=4]Usage[/size][/b]

Select a vanilla shelf and open its Storage tab. Enter a number beside any resource to set its maximum. Clear the field to remove the limit.
If the shelf already contains more than the selected maximum, pawns can haul the excess to another valid storage destination. Another storage location must accept that resource and have free space.


[b][size=4]Compatibility[/size][/b]

Shelf Limiter uses Harmony patches and does not replace vanilla definitions. Mods that heavily rewrite the storage-filter interface or hauling logic may require compatibility work.


[b][size=4]Source Code and Bug Reports[/size][/b]

[list]
[*][url=https://github.com/kolop049/Shelf-Limiter][/url][url=https://github.com/kolop049/Shelf-Limiter]https://github.com/kolop049/Shelf-Limiter[/url][/*]
[/list]Please report bugs through GitHub or the Nexus Mods posts section.

[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
Nothing is 100% "required" but I do recommend some other mods this was designed around, it will probably work without them but contains some .xml addressing them also so it will probably throw some harmless red error logs on start:

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1503448404]In-wall coolers and vents[/url] + [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3286518227]Wall Heater[/url]

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2591816333]Optimization: Leathers - C# Edition[/url]

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2890901044]Combat Extended[color=#ffffff] + [/color][/url][color=#ffffff][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3456155186] [/url][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3771552493]Combat Skills Matter More (Nerfed Version, Revised For Combat Extended)[/url] [/color]


[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2890901044][color=#ffffff][b][size=5]Recommendations[/size][/b][/color][/url]
More recommendations not mentioned in my files:

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2890901044][/url][color=#ffffff][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2950042909][HB] Pemmican 2.0 Reskin
[/url]

[size=5][b]Description[/b][/size][/color]
This mod is 100% .xml only. You can enter any one to remove/modify/add whatever you want, or you could even delete entire files/folders to remove whatever you want for example if you don't have a specific mentioned mod.

The "universal maths" behind my mod is the idea that:
Every unit of fabric/leather weighs 0.1 kg.
Every unit of wood/stone/metal is 1 kg however it is divided or multiplied depending on use scale or balance case. For example if individual armor weighs 15 kg then we imagine that it is divided by 10 so 150 units of metal is needed to make 15 kg armor. For some furniture/structures then we imagine that it is multiplied by 10 or 100, for example it takes 5 units of material to make a 1 square meter wall, we simply imagine it is 500 kg of material, it is not as though our pawns have to carry 500 units of material to build 1 wall.[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2890901044]
[/url]Every 5 units of wood burned per day generates 24 heat per second so it is as if burning 5 units of wood is 10 times more at 50 kg of wood for burning. Every 10 units of wood burned is equivalent to 2000 watts for 1 day so a wood burning generator consuming 20 wood per day at 50% efficiency generates 2000 watts per day while the other half, 10/20 units of wood turns into waste heat.

Unfortunately RimWorld doesn't accept ".xslt" files for modding so I can't make this mod a little smaller and more effective. If it accepted .xslt files I could replace some fixed values with some formulas instead that would calculate the values of many things at 1% file size.
For example if I could use .xslt then I could make a mathematical formula to calculate the material cost of weapons based on their stats. Same for armor, same for buildings.
I would be able to calculate the stats of plants based on their other stats.
It would make it possible for me to use a few mathematical formulas to do the same as creating .xml files with thousands of addressed Defs. Unfortunately RimWorld doesn't accept .xslt files like Bannerlord so it's more bloated.


[b][size=5]Defs/[/size][/b]
[size=4]Recipe_RealisticOmnivorePemmican[/size]
Adds a new omnivore pemmican recipe that uses a small amount of plant ingredients since the main recipe is now 100% carnivorous.

[size=4]Simplify_Recipe_Stone[/size]
[color=#d4d4d8]Make granite blocks from other stone blocks since this mod aims to use Granite only.[/color]

[color=#d4d4d8][size=4]Simplify_Scorpio.OptimizationLeathers[/size][/color]
[color=#d4d4d8]Adds a new stuff category for chitin from "Optimization: Leathers" which can only be used for makeable outer layers like parkas and jackets.[/color]

[color=#d4d4d8][size=4]Simplify_Terrain_Foundation [/size][/color]
[color=#d4d4d8]Adds 2 new bridges to the game, stone "granite bridge" and the metal "steel bridge". Unfortunately I'm still using the graphics from the native game so that means while the top of the bridges has the looks of granite tiles and steel tiles the bottom legs are still wooden props from the native wood bridge.[/color]


[color=#d4d4d8][size=5][b]Patches/[/b][/size][/color]
[size=4][b]NoBulkRecipes/[/b][/size]
Same as my [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/rimworld/mods/692]No Bulk Recipes For Food[/url] mod.


[size=4][b]RealisticPemmican/[/b][/size]
Same as my [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/rimworld/mods/691]Realistic Pemmican[/url] mod.


[b][size=4]Simplify - CETeam.CombatExtended/[/size][/b]
[size=4]Simplify_Apparel_Various[/size]
Replaced the "Steeled" stuff category CE creates back to normal "Metallic". I found it too limiting.
Since CE makes flak armor stuffable with fabric I replaced that with metals instead. I found it stupid that flak armor was made with a variety of fabric instead of a variety of metals. To simulate flak armor being plate carriers.

[size=4]Simplify_CombatExtended.CompProperties_FireModes[/size]
I can't remember where I found this stat from but this file removes the effect "CombatExtended.CompProperties_FireModes" from Combat Extended so players no longer have fire modes with ranged weapons. Because I didn't like the extra bloat and micro-management. I wish pawns were smart enough to use different fire modes and bipods automatically.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource_Stuff[/size]
Removes all CE's mass multipliers for resources which created variations in mass. Now the mass of all items is the same, to simulate  for example if a material is denser then engineers simply use it more thinly, if a material is denser then engineers simply use it more thickly like in real life.

[size=4]Simplify_Stats_Pawns_Combat[/size]
The " AimingAccuracy" stat created by Combat Extended has been highly modified so that level 0~1 shooters with this mod should be equivalent to level 17~18 shooters without this mod, hopefully this means no more firing 10 bullets into the wall while enemies are charging towards you in a straight corridor 10 meters away.

[size=4]Simplify_Weapons_Grenades[/size]
Replaces the 1 second cooldown time after throwing a grenade to "3" seconds. I found it stupid how many grenades were being thrown quickly by pawns with Combat Extended.

[size=4]Simplify_Weapons_Guns[/size]
Removes bipod options from CE to reduce micro-management.
The ranged cooldown time for few weapons under 0.66 seconds has been increased to 0.66 so pawns' fingers aren't acting so robotic.
Weapons that use .303 British ammo now use 7.62 NATO ammo to simplify ammo management in CE.
Increased the magazine capacity of the sniper rifle to "10" to match the bolt-action rifle so it's not a worse weapon.


[size=4][b]Simplify - Dylan.CSL - Children, school and learning/[/b][/size]
Currently an empty folder because I can't figure out how to mod and simplify this mod without creating any errors.


[size=4][b]Simplify_Apparel/[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_Apparel_Headgear[/size]
Allows the war mask to be made of leather and fabric. I found it dumb it could only be made from wood.
Reduces the cost of the "simple helmet" made of metal to be 20 units of metal since it only weighs 2 kg.

[size=4]Simplify_Apparel_Various[/size]
Removed plate armor from being allowed to be made of wood. I found it dumb since medieval people didn't make "wooden plate armor" to fight and it bloated the storage.
Like my [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/rimworld/mods/699]Apparel Fix[/url] except with more features. Removed the "Shell/Outer" layer, kept the middle layer for plate armor so now you can wear plate armor under a duster like NCR veteran rangers.

[b][img width=712]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/424/images/699/699-1783247148-624575281.png[/img][/b]

Removed the "Middle" layer from flak pants so that we no longer have to annoyingly drop pants everytime we put on heavy armor or get butt naked everytime we take off heavy armor.
Quality has been removed from apparel just like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/rimworld/mods/738]No Quality For Equipment[/url].



[size=4][b]Simplify_Buildings/[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_Buildings[/size]
Changes all beds' rest effectiveness to "1" so there's no more magical beds that make you require more/less sleep. The only difference between different beds should be the comfort and beauty of the beds.
All beds' "ImmunityGainSpeedFactor", "MedicalTendQualityOffset", "SurgerySuccessChanceFactor" should be the same at "1" base value now. Now more magic beds that somehow make you recover faster, medicine become more effective or surgery become more effective.
Set all "heatPushMaxTemperature" to 25 degrees. Your pawns should be smart enough to regulate the temperature of a wooden torch or campfire to avoid being too hot for comfort.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Furniture[/size]
Sets "bed_healPerDay" for all beds to be the same. Now no more magical beds that make you heal faster or slower.
The "stuffCategories" of beds have been changes so that now beds are made of fabric or leather just like bedrolls. (I couldn't decide if I wanted to add wood/steel or not.)
The "costStuffCount" of furniture has been changes to reflect universal maths. The idea is that every unit of fabric/leather is 0.1 kg and every unit of wood/stone/metal for building is 10 kg or 100 kg.
The 3x3 table is now hidden for the player since it's the stupidest table because it has 1 empty square meter in the middle.
Hide standing wood torches for the player, now wall torches is the only wooden torch in the architect menu.
Fuel consumption of the wall torch has been modified to reflect new maths.
The heat production of wooden wall torches has been updated to reflect real physics. Now wood no longer magically disappears into less/more heat energy depending on where it is burnt.
The electric standing lamp has also been hidden and only the wall electric lamp is visible to the player in the architect menu.
The electric lamps have been updated to produce heat proportional to their energy consumption.
Inspired by the tables and annoyed by vanilla shelves I've decided to make shelves symmetrical. In vanilla RimWorld it doesn't matter what side of the shelf you're facing as long as it is 1 tile away to reach so there's no point in it having asymmetrical graphics.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Joy[/size]
Out of the 4 basic recreation buildings: Horseshoes and Game of Ur are now hidden, it is simply hoopstones and chess tables only now.
" JoyGainFactor" has all been set to "1" so this means that certain recreation buildings aren't more or less effective per second than others.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Misc[/size]
The Tool Cabinet's hit points and cost has now been balanced to reflect being a 400 kg unit of steel.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Natural[/size]
I thought it was stupid that almost every natural in the environent pawns hated. Now natural rock/mountain walls have "1" beauty so pawns should slightly appreciate natural beautiful mountains and hills.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Power[/size]
Conduits have been simplified so there is only 2 variants, the hidden and waterproof, no more basic low quality conduits. They both have the same units of steel cost to build.
Wood generators have their power output increased to "2000" watts because I thought 1000 watts was an inadaquete amount of power considering they burn through 20 units of wood per day, even considering 50% efficiency.
Batteries now stores more watt days of power per unit instead of 600 which seemed like an arbitrary number to me. And their "efficiency" is now 100% since the game doesn't have waste heat for batteries I didn't want energy magically disappearing. Though I did create a small heat output for batteries because they discharge 5 watts waste.
The hit points of several power buildings has been highly increased to be more realistic and reasonable relative to their steel cost and size. Bigger power buildings that require dozens/hundreds of units of steel presumabily weighs hundreds or thousands of kilograms so they shouldn't just disappear after a few bullets. Shooting a large metal generator should feel like shooting at multiple metal walls.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Production[/size]
Stoves now produce 24 heat per second (0.40 heat per tick), same as the campfires, because we can't magically cook food with little/no heat. Also balances the fueled stove to consume 5 units of wood per day and the electric stove to consume 1,000 watts per day. Obviously the real consumption will be less since they aren't used 100% of the time, they only consume wood/power when cooking.
The "NutrientPasteDispenser" and "Hopper" has been hidden from the player becuase I disagree with their existence.
More work benches can be made from different materials now. So now you can have granite stoves for example.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Security[/size]
Reduces the work time to build of trap spikes to be much more reasonable. Work time has been replaced with the same value as making an IED. Since spike traps cost 45 units of metal/stone we are imagining it is a 45 kg contraption.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Structure + Simplify_GT.Sam.BasicDoubleDoors[/size]
The costs of structures has been balanced so that this aren't as disproportionately more/less than others. Doors no longer cost 5 times more than a wall. A fence gate no longer costs 25 times more than a fence.
Columns because they are large and strong structures have 50% cover instead of 25%. Going past columns slows pawns down like trees instead of letting pawns magically phase through them. Columns have more hit points and less cost to make them more realistic relative to walls and how they exist in real life.

[size=4]Simplify_Buildings_Temperature + Simplify_Xercaine.WallHeater[/size]
The consumption and capacity of campfires has been halves. Using new maths to calculate the heat output.
Campfires take the same amount of time to cook as stoves, I found it stupid that campfires cooked slower than stoves.
The heater and Xercaine's wall heater no longer require 10 times as much steel as a wall. The power consumption of heaters has been increased to 1,000 watts to reflect better physics and maths.
The vent no longer costs 6 times as much steel as a wall.


[b][size=4]Simplify_Hediffs/[/size][/b]
[size=4]Simplify_Hediffs_BodyParts_Natural[/size]
The value of lungs and kidneys are halved, now the liver is worth slightly less than a heart so they no longer have the same value.

[size=4]Simplify_Hediffs_Global_Misc[/size]
Trying to nerf food poisoning.

[size=4]Simplify_Hediffs_Global_Needs[/size]
Made a slightly randomised range of 4+ times the amount of time needed for pawns to starve to death of malnutrition. I thought it was stupid that in the vanilla game after just a couple days of fighting without food one of my fighters would just starve to death in bed at a fixed time. In real life humans can last anywhere from weeks to months without food and people don't die of starvation at the exact same time with no variation. Even considering 5 days in RimWorld is equivalent to 1 month in real life, pawns were dying too stupidly quick.
The death risk of malnutirition is much lower but the other risks are higher.  Moving,  Manipulation and Consciousness are now all effected by malnutrition. Pawns get much weaker before they die of malnutrition.

[size=4]Simplify_Hediffs_Local_Infections[/size]
"Flu" has now been nerfed so that it no longer has a 99% fatality rate on untended patients. I thought it was stupid how high the death risk for the flu was for untended patients. The basic immunity rate for the flu is now slightly higher than the severity rate, only the unhealthiest pawns can die of the flu based on the new values.
Wound infections immunity rate is now slightly higher to fill half the gap between the immunity rate and lethality rate. Now too many pawns/prisoners shouldn't die so easily from infections but it is still very dangerous if the patient's health is bad and the wound is untreated. Most people willl still die if the infection is untended and/or if their liver and kidneys are in poor health, but it feels like it's much more possible to survive it now.


[size=4][b]Simplify_Items/[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_Items_Food[/size]
The weight of meals has been standardised to "0.5" kg instead of being 0.44 kg which seemed arbitrary.
"Packaged survival meal" now has a spoilage time of 2 years, double pemmican instead of being magically spoil-proof.
Fine meal now takes the same amount of work to make as a simple meal because the amount of ingredients required is the same, the only difference is the mixture of ingredients so it shouldn't waste more time.
" Kibble" now has a spoilage time of 1 year, it should be dried feed, not magical never spoiling feed.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource[/size]
" FoodPoisonChanceFixedHuman" has been removed from all food in the hopes of removing food poisoning from the game.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource_AnimalProduct[/size]
Milk because it is liquid now has a mass of "0.1" to make it heavier than dry food.
Eggs' nutrition values have been modified to try to make it less buggy since the game wastes eggs often due to their high nutrition value per unit. For example if an egg has 0.5 or 0.6 nutrition but a recipe requried 0.25 nutrition from eggs then the extra 0.25/0.35 nutrition is wasted, even when I set eggs' nutrition down to 0.10 nutrition they will still waste it by using 3 eggs or if nutrition is 0.20 then they will waste it by using 2 eggs. I'm trying to fix this bug with my mod.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource_Base[/size]
The base beauty of resources has been set to "-1" from vanilla "-4". I find it stupid that pawns find stacks of resources to be relatively uglier than some other things.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource_Manufactured[/size]
Removes basic deterioration from components, advanced components and reinforced barrels since they are metallic non-organic resources.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource_RawPlant[/size]
All raw plant ingredients now have "0.05" mass (50 grams) instead of the seemingly arbitrary 0.03 mass (30 grams) for some reason.

[size=4]Simplify_Items_Resource_Stuff + Simplify_Items_Resource_Stuff_Leather[/size]
The mass of silver and gold per unit is now 10 grams instead of being 8 grams which seemed arbitrary.
All metals, stones, wood is now 1 kg per unit. Except for silver/gold.
All textiles including fabrics, wool, leather is now 0.1 kg per unit to prepare for universal maths.
Flammability of silver, gold and steel is now "0" so that means they should behave like metal now, no longer magically set on fire as if they are made of organic material like wood or fuel.
Gold is now 50 times more valuable than silver per unit/mass.
Steel's material hit point multiplier is now "2.1" which is a lot higher than stone now, steel walls should now be stronger than stone walls.
Plasteel's sharp damage multiplier is now much lower since it's supposed to be highly similar to plastic, it's like trying to stab someone with a plastic/kevlar knife, it's too lightweight and not hard enough, it should only be good for armor.
The "commonality" of "Synthread" has been set to 0.00" because it's not a good material, it just adds extra bloat to the game.
The "commonality" of all wool has been set to "0.00" to hopefully make them stop spawning.
The heat insulation value of muffalo wool and bluefur has been balanced to avoid muffalo just being overpowered bison.


[size=4][b]Simplify_Plants_Wild/[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_Plants_Bases[/size]
Most plants can now grow in minimum 30% light instead of vanilla 51%.

[size=4]Simplify_Plants_Cultivated_Farm[/size]
Removes growing skills requirements from all plants because I thought it looked stupid farmers who can grow corn, potatoes, rice can't grow trees. Increased the time to grow and yield of faster growing crops to reduce the gap between them and corn which was massive.
Strawberry plants have been modified to not die on harvest just like wild berry bushes and in real life. So now they can re-grow.
Strawberry bushes have been nerfed to reduce harvest yield and increase growing time to balance them since they no longer need re-planting after every harvest. Same for Healroot.
The "Flammability" of devilstrand has been set to 0.4, because I found it stupid a highly effective fire and pierce-resistant fungus was very vulnerable to small fires.

[size=4]Simplify_Plants_Wild[/size]
Modified "tall grass" so that they're not so massively and magically different from normal grass.


[size=4][b]Simplify_Races/
[/b]Simplify_Races_Animal[/size]
Reduced the herd group size of animals to reduce the game's bug of a large herd of animals all turning manhunter at the same time.
Set farm animals to wander off on average only once every 10 years, so now it should be easier to graze across your home.
Disabled some birds magically not laying eggs when not fertilized.
Increased the shearable time to be 59 days instead of 10-15 days like in vanilla to make shearing more relaistic but also created another part to disable all animals from producing wool.
Made it so that herbivores can also eat trees. I found it dumb that herbivorous animals don't eat the leaves of trees for some reason. Unfortunately the game doesn't consider the height and quantity of leaves on a tree so it does look strange sometimes.

[size=4]Simplify_Races_Animal_ChickenGroup[/size]
Chickens, ducks, turkeys, geese are now omnivores like in real life instead of herbivores.
Made chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese in that order more unique by giving them more and different cold weather resistance in 5 degree increments/decrements.

[size=4]Simplify_Races_Animal_CowGroup[/size]
Muffalo and bison have been balanced so that muffalo isn't just an overpowered version of the bison. More of these mammals can now produce milk.

[size=4]Simplify_Races_Animal_PigGroup[/size]
Pigs and boars can now hunt very small animals up to a maximum of "0.16" body size because I found it stupid that hungry pigs/boars didn't already do that to much smaller animals.
Ibex, Deer, Gazelle now produce milk also.

[size=4]Simplify_Races_Animal_SheepGroup[/size]
Sheep, Alpaca, Megasloth now produce milk also.

[size=4]Simplify_Races_Humanlike[/size]
Butchering humans now gives 0 "LeatherAmount" to hopefully get rid of human leather from the game. The idea is that cannibals are eating even skin because practically the leather of non-furry and thinner skinned animals such as humans and pigs don't make good leather.


[size=4][b]Simplify_Recipes/[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_Recipes_Food[/size]
Kibble has been balanced to be meat only.
Kibble recipe has been hidden from the player because I thought it was unrealistic since both herbivorous and carnivorous animals could eat kibble.

[size=4]Simplify_Recipes_Meals[/size]
The ingredients cost to make meals has been increased to that cooking a meal doesn't magically give 80% more nutrition than eating fresh ingredients.
Also RimWorld has a bug with pawns using eggs for cooking and wasting extra nutrition I'm trying to fix with this file.
"Fine meal" has been balanced to use animal products with meat/plants, instead of meat/animal products with plants so now animal products is a 100% essential ingredient for fine meals instead of being an alternative to meat.
All specific vegetarian/carnivorous meals and lavish meals cooking has been hidden from the player.

[size=4]Simplify_Recipes_Production[/size]
Since steel slag is made to weigh the same as stone chunks, the units of material produced has been made the same also.


[b][size=4]Simplify_Stats/[/size][/b]
[size=4]Simplify_Stats_Building_Special[/size]
The "BedRestEffectiveness" for different quality beds is now all "1". This means no more magical beds that makes higher quality beds require humans/animals to need less/more sleep. The benefits of different quality is now only in the other stats. not magical biology.

[size=4]Simplify_Stats_Pawns_General[/size]
The defName "RestRateMultiplier" has been set to "1". I have no idea what it does but I'm hoping that it makes sleeping anywhere is as effective as sleeping in bed.

[size=4]Simplify_Stats_Pawns_WorkGeneral[/size]
"MiningYield", "AnimalGatherYield", "PlantHarvestYield" for all skill levels is now "1". So high skilled pawns won't magically make more resources and low skilled pawns won't magically make less resources.
Health status should only effect the speed of mining/gathering/harvesting, it should no longer magically effect how much resources is gained.

[size=4]Simplify_Stats_Pawns_WorkRecipes[/size]
The "FoodPoisonChance" for all skill levels has been set to "0" to hopefully remove food poisoning from the game.
"ButcheryFleshEfficiency" and "ButcheryMechanoidEfficiency" has been set to "1" and gains 0 bonus per skill level so different skilled pawns don't magically make less or more resources from butchering animals and mechanoids. Now the difference is only in the speed.


[size=4][b]Simplify_Terrain/[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_Terrain_Fertility[/size]
The "fertility" of multiple terrain has been replaced so that soft sand can support some plants just like dry sand, mud and marsh can actually support some very low fertility requirement plants. So now you shouldn't see barren marshes anymore.

[size=4]Simplify_Terrain_Floors[/size]
"FilthMultiplier" for all terrain has been removed. Now certain floors don't magically receive more/less filth.
"Concrete" and "PavedTile" has been hidden for the player.
To make things more progressive, with wooden tiles requiring 2 seconds (120 ticks) of work to build as the standard, (stone tiles 4 seconds in another file), metal tiles require 8 seconds of work, sterile tiles require 16 seconds of work. A doubling for every level of flooring.
Wodden floors now have "1" beauty so your ungrateful pawns will actually appreciate beautiful wooden floors.
Silver and gold tiles now need a little bit of steel as well as silver or gold to build as "structural support".

[size=4]Simplify_Terrain_Floors_Stone[/size]
Stone tiles now require less work to build, have 1 beauty.
All non-granite stone tiles have been hidden.
Granite stone tiles color has been changed to make it more unique.
All flagstones have been hidden for the player. We only need 1 stone floor type to avoid bloating the game.

[size=4]Simplify_Terrain_Foundation[/size]
2nd Simplify_Terrain_Foundation file in Patches instead of the Defs folder to patch the normal bridge to fit with the new added bridges.
Bridges now have "1" beauty so your ungrateful pawns will now appreciate beautiful bridges over water views.


[b][size=4]Simplify_Thoughts/[/size][/b]
[size=4]Simplify_Thoughts_Memory_Death[/size]
Pawns now gain 1 mood instead of losing when a guilty pawn is killed. The new description is now "A guilty prisoner or guest was executed. It was justified."
Mood loss is now only for innocent prisoners/guests dying.

[size=4]Simplify_Thoughts_Memory_Eating[/size]
Reduced mood effect from eating meals made from human meat, they still complain but less than eating meals made from insect meat at least.

[size=4]Simplify_Thoughts_Memory_Misc[/size]
"AteWithoutTable" mood loss is now just 9 hours instead of complaining about that for 24 hours and the mood effect is only "-1" which is a lot more reasonable.
"KnowPrisonerSold" mood effect is now only "-1" since the game doesn't differentiate whether a prisoner deserves to be sold or not.
"KnowGuestOrganHarvested", "ButcheredHumanlikeCorpse", "KnowButcheredHumanlikeCorpse", "ObservedLayingCorpse", "ObservedLayingRottingCorpse" all have their mood effects including their stacks reduced. Now they won't complain as much.

[size=4]Simplify_Thoughts_Situation_Special[/size]
Removes the mood effect from leaving colonists unburied. Mood loss from seeing corpses is enough, unburied people shouldn't create a dumb domino effect of mood loss.

[size=4]Simplify_Thoughts_Situation_Traits[/size]
Reduce the mood effect from nudists wearing clothes to "0" to make nudists less stupid. They gain mood from being nude but they don't lose mood from not being nude.


[b][size=4]Simplify_Weapons/[/size][/b]
[size=4]Simplify_BaseWeapons[/size]
Removes quality modifiers for guns, sharp weapons and blunt weapons. Same as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/rimworld/mods/738]No Quality For Equipment[/url].

[size=4]Simplify_Ranged[/size]
The "warmupTime" which is the aiming time of all weapons has been set to "0.8" seconds. Now when someone with a machine gun or sniper rifle paces against someone with a pistol they won't stand in front of them like an idiot for 2 seconds while getting shot. I specifically chose 0.8 seconds because it's a nice even number that other skill multipliers and mods can halve to 0.4 seconds and then halve again to 0.2 seconds.

[size=4]Simplify_RangedIndustrial[/size]
The range of industrial guns has now been increased to 100-200 meters based on key words.
The revolver and autopistol now have their "RangedWeapon_Cooldown" which is the inverse of rate of fire set to "0.66" seconds which means 1.5 shots per second, This leaves room for a mod that reduces the time to half at 0.33 seconds allowing for 3 shots per second.
[youtube]Z0wL6DXIvoc[/youtube]

[size=4]Simplify_RangedMechanoid[/size]
All ranged mechanoids should now have 200 meters range. No one should be able to outrange mechanoids now. Should make Mechanoids much harder to fight, especially with Combat Extended.

[size=4]Simplify_RangedNeolithic[/size]
[size=3]Quality modifiers removed from neolithic weapons also.[/size]
[size=3]Bows and pilum ranges increased.[/size]


[size=4][b]Loose Files:[/b][/size]
[size=4]Simplify_BackstoryDefs[/size]
All "workDisables" for pawns' bacstories has been replaced with "None". Now no more stupid work restrictions. I wanted to mod the thousands of backstories with .xslt to make it result in skill losses as well but RimWorld doesn't accept .xslt .

[size=4]Simplify_Designations[/size]
Smoothing walls, floors, surfaces are now hidden for the player because smoothing is a waste of time.

[size=4]Simplify_Races_Humanlike[/size]
The comfortable temperature range for humans is now 12 to 28 degrees, so 20 is the mid point instead of the base game's 16 to 26 degrees with 21 being the mid point. It's nice even numbers now and pawns don't complain so much about it being slightly cold and just 27 degrees warmth.

[size=4]Simplify_ResearchProject[/size]
The dumb positioning of "Mortars" in the research tree has been fixed. Since mortars need machining tables to make it comes after machining now.

[size=4]Simplify_Roofs[/size]
Both the rock and mountain roof has the same stats to make mountain bases simpler.

[size=4]Simplify_Scorpio.OptimizationLeathers[/size]
Patch version of this file to make "Optimization: Leathers".

[size=4]Simplify_ThinkTreeDefs [/size]
Perform the function of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3350217733]No Carried Food (Continued)[/url] but that mod always gave me an error message on start up and didn't work for me so I created this new one.

[size=4]Simplify_Traits[/size]
The spawn rate of nudists and body modders has been massively reduced because I found it stupid how common they were in the game.
The "Gourmand" trait no longer has pawns eating 50% more food magically.

[size=4]Simplify_Various_Stone[/size]
Stone chunks on the floor now provide 25% cover instead of 50% which was over effective considering the mass and size.
Every square meter of stone being mined now drops 1 chunk instead of it being random chance if stone disappears magically or not.
Stone chunks now weigh a whopping 21 kg since they produce 20 units of stone blocks weighing 1 kg each. Same for steel slags.
Granite as with stone tiles now have a much whiter color. Whiter granite is used to differentiate it from all other stones and metals.
The beauty of smoothed surfaces has been set to "1" so your ungreateful pawns appreciate it, though I disabled it in this mod anyway.
All stone blocks set to 1 kg.
Same as the terrain file the beauty of rock has been set to "1" so pawns appreciate beautiful rocky mountains and hills.
Granite has the same beauty multiplier as marble now since it's replacing it. All stone blocks other than granite has been hidden from being made by the player. Now all stone chunks only creates granite blocks.
The commonality of non-granite and non-jade stone has been set to "0.00" to make them less common of course now.
The "WorkToBuild" and "WorkToMake" multipliers for granite blocks has been reduced to "1.0" like steel because it was ridiculous how they were multiple times longer than making steel things.


I really wanted to use and design my mod around [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2076686656]Mixed Stone Blocks[/url] because it aims to add/replace stone blocks with beautiful mixed bricks but unfortunately it's too buggy to work.

nodes.name: Buy Anything
nodes.summary: BuyAnything adds a fully configurable merchant terminal to RimWorld. Buy and sell almost any item, receive purchases instantly or by cargo pods, generate blueprint shopping reports for construction projects, customize taxes and pricing, and
nodes.description:
[b][size=6]BuyAnything[/size][/b]
[size=4][b]Any Item. Anytime. Delivered.[/b][/size]
[size=4]Tired of waiting for the perfect trade caravan to show up with the one item your colony desperately needs?
[b]BuyAnything[/b] introduces a fully configurable [b]Merchant Terminal[/b] that allows you to buy and sell almost any item in RimWorld through a clean, intuitive shopping interface. Whether you're replacing a broken component, stocking up on medicine before a raid, ordering thousands of units of steel for a massive construction project, or instantly hiring colony-wide services, BuyAnything streamlines your colony's logistics while remaining fully customizable.
Whether you're running a tiny frontier settlement or a late-game industrial empire, BuyAnything gives you the tools to keep your colony supplied, automate tedious tasks, and keep your projects moving.[/size]
[line]
[b][size=6]Features:[/size][/b]
[heading][size=5]🛒 Buy & Sell[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Purchase almost any item available in RimWorld through an easy-to-use shopping interface.[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]🛒 Buy almost any item in the game [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]💰 Sell items directly from your colony [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]📦 Choose between Instant Delivery or Cargo Pod Delivery [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]📊 Detailed shopping cart with subtotal, tax, and total cost [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]⚙ Adjustable pricing, taxes, purchase limits, and delivery options [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🚀 Smart cargo pod delivery that avoids roofs and structures whenever possible [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🔍 Fast searching and organized item categories [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🎨 Clean, RimWorld-style user interface [/size][/*]
[/list][line]
[b][size=5]🏗 Blueprint Purchasing[/size][/b]
[size=4]Planning a large construction project has never been easier.[/size]
[size=4]Simply scan your construction blueprints to generate a complete shopping report showing:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Required materials [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Materials already in storage [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Missing resources [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Individual item costs [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Purchase subtotal [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Estimated tax [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Grand total [/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Purchase materials individually or add the entire report directly to your shopping cart with a single click.[/size]

[line]
[size=5][b]⚡ Colony Services[/b][/size]
[size=4]Need work done immediately? Hire specialized colony services directly from the Merchant Terminal.[/size]
[size=4]Current services include:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]🧹 Clean Colony [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]☠ Remove Bodies [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🪨 Remove Chunks [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]📦 Auto Haul [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🌲 Harvest Trees [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🌾 Harvest Crops [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]⛏ Mine Designated Areas [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🏗 Finish Construction [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]🔧 Repair Buildings [/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Every service has its own configurable silver cost and can be individually enabled or disabled in the mod settings, allowing you to balance convenience however you like.[/size]

[line]
[b][size=6]⚙[/size][/b][size=6] Highly Configurable[/size]
[size=4]BuyAnything is designed to fit your playstyle.[/size]
[size=4]Customize options such as:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Buy price multiplier [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Sell price multiplier [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Trade tax [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Purchase limits [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Instant or cargo pod delivery [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Research requirements [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Power requirements [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Pawn interaction requirements [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Negative silver allowance [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Individual Colony Service pricing [/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Individual service enable/disable options [/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Whether you want a simple quality-of-life improvement or a balanced trading experience, the choice is yours.[/size]

[line]
[b][size=5]🔧 Compatibility[/size][/b]
[size=4]BuyAnything is designed to work alongside heavily modded playthroughs by building its catalog directly from the game's item definitions. Mod-added items are supported automatically whenever possible, allowing the Merchant Terminal to scale with your mod list without requiring individual compatibility patches.[/size]
[line]
[b][size=5]Why BuyAnything?[/size][/b]
[size=4]Trade caravans are great for storytelling—but not always for logistics.[/size]
[size=4]BuyAnything removes the frustration of waiting days for a trader that may never bring what you need, letting you spend more time building, surviving, and expanding your colony.[/size]
[size=4]From purchasing a single advanced component to supplying an entire megabase with construction materials or automating routine colony tasks, BuyAnything gives you the flexibility to play RimWorld your way.[/size]
[line]
[size=6]Buy Anything 1.0 — Trade Contracts & Progression Update[/size]
[size=4]Buy Anything 1.0 turns the terminal into a full progression and trading system, with contracts, merchant reputation, quality-of-life tools, and major stability fixes.[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Added a complete contract gameplay loop:
[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Accept contracts[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Gather the requested goods[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Track colony inventory progress[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Deliver the goods[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Receive silver by cargo pod[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Earn merchant reputation[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Get replacement contracts[/size][/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][size=4]Added accepted-contract tracking, expiration, delivery validation, and automatic failure/replacement for expired contracts.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Added five contract types:
[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Procurement[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Rush Orders[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Bulk Orders[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Emergency Aid[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Prototype Orders[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Construction Projects[/size][/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][size=4]Added themed contractor requests:
[/size]

nodes.name: Rimzone
nodes.summary: Vanilla zoning is too flat. Rimzone completely replaces it, letting your zones decide who enters! Set rules on zones to restrict access by skill rank, social group, or active work priorities. Features smart bypasses for medical/emergencies.
nodes.description:
Disclaimer: All mechanics of the mod are finished but, I have not yet put the mod through extensive in-game testing and there may be bugs I have not yet seen. If you encounter any bugs please include enough detail for me to be able to track down the problem. Include your mod list, zone settings, pawn skills and work priorities (if using those options), as well as a description of the bug. Screenshots can also be helpful.

Rimzone: System Overhaul (Alpha)
Have you ever found the vanilla zoning system to be a bit too flat and limited? Managing large colonies often turns into a tedious chore of micromanaging dozens of custom areas, manually assigning and reassigning pawns every time their skills improve, their jobs change, or an emergency hits.

[b]Rimzone[/b] is a complete, bottom-up overhaul of RimWorld’s zoning architecture [1.6]. Instead of the traditional loop of assigning a static zone to a pawn, [b]Rimzone turns the system on its head: you set the rules on the zones themselves, and the zones dynamically decide who is allowed inside, when, and for what purpose.[/b]
[line]
[heading]Key Features[/heading]
Dynamic Work Priority Access
Configure your production hubs, defensive bunkers, or mining areas to only allow pawns with active work assignments.
[list]
[*][b]Compatibility:[/b] Whether you use [b]Complex Jobs[/b], custom work type mods, or increased priority rank mods (supporting up to 10 priority levels), Rimzone dynamically reads the active jobs and lists them.[/*]
[/list]Access by Skill Rank & Passion
Keep your low-skill, low-passion pawns out of high-waste environments. You can restrict your kitchen to chefs with a cooking skill of 8+, block clumsy pawns from advanced crafting benches, or reserve clean laboratories for your top researchers.
[list]
[*][b]Compatibility:[/b] Dynamically detects and adapts to custom skills added or removed by other mods.[/*]
[/list]Smart Bypass Exceptions (Emergency Tasks)
Exclusion zones are great, but fire and structural collapses don't care about zoning rules. Rimzone features six toggleable task bypasses. You can keep a zone completely locked down, or allow any pawn to bypass the restriction temporarily to perform vital duties:
[list]
[*][b]Firefighting:[/b] Anyone can run in to douse a fire.[/*]
[*][b]Construction & Repairs:[/b] Handymen can enter to build blueprints or repair walls.[/*]
[*][b]Dropoff & Pickup:[/b] Haulers can access restricted stockpiles and storage buildings to grab or drop off resources.[/*]
[*][b]Medical Care:[/b] Doctors and rescuers can enter any zone to tend to sick, bedridden, or downed patients.[/*]
[/list]Fine-Grained Social Toggles
Quickly lock down or open up zones based on pawn categories. Toggle access instantly for:
[list]
[*][b]Colonists[/b][/*]
[*][b]Slaves[/b][/*]
[*][b]Prisoners[/b][/*]
[*][b]Animals[/b][/*]
[*][b]Raid Blockades:[/b] Block pawn access to specific outdoor or high-risk zones automatically when the map danger rating spikes to High.[/*]
[/list]Custom Pawn Whitelisting
Rules are meant to be broken. If a pawn fails a zone's skill or work filters but you still need them to have access, you can manually add them to the zone’s individual whitelist with a single click to bypass all dynamic restrictions.
[line]
[heading]How It Works[/heading]
[list=1]
[*][b]Place your zone[/b] (such as home, or a custom area) using the standard area architect tools.[/*]
[*][b]Open the Rimzone Editor[/b] from the area settings.[/*]
[*][b]Configure your parameters:[/b] check off which categories of pawns are allowed, set minimum skills, and check off work requirements.[/*]
[*][b]Let the mod do the rest:[/b] Pawns will automatically respect the boundaries based on their real-time state, re-routing as their skills, priorities, or drafting statuses change.[/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]Installation Instructions[/heading]
[list=1]
[*][b]Required Dependency:[/b] Ensure you have [b]Harmony[/b] installed and loaded at the very top of your mod list.[/*]
[*][b]Mod Placement:[/b] Place [b]Rimzone[/b] after [b]Core[/b], any official [b]DLCs[/b], and [b]Harmony[/b], but before any mods that heavily alter pathfinding behaviors (though it is designed to be highly compatible with most common performance and pathfinding tools).[/*]
[*][b]Mid-Save Compatibility:[/b] Rimzone can be safely added to an ongoing save game. To be absolutely safe, it is highly recommended to make a backup of your save file before activating any major system overhaul.[/*]
[/list]

nodes.summary: This entry in the More Birds series populates your beaches, marshes, and riverbanks with a diverse collection of water-loving avian fauna. From small, frantic shorebirds darting across the sand to towering, majestic waders hunting out in
nodes.description:
[color=#D4D4D8][b][size=5]FROM THE 'MORE BIRDS' SERIES OF MODS[/size][/b]
Want more birds? [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/11Bullets/mods]CLICK HERE![/url]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ydAv9tb.gif[/img]

[size=4]Bring the magnificent wildlife of coastlines and wetlands to your colony![/size]
This entry in the [b][i]More Birds[/i][/b] series populates your beaches, marshes, and riverbanks with a diverse collection of water-loving avian fauna. From small, frantic shorebirds darting across the sand to towering, majestic waders hunting out in the shallows, these birds add visual depth and realism to your colony's waterways.

Whether hunting them for their meat, harvesting their beautiful feathers for high-status tribal apparel, or domesticating them as prestigious companions for your throne halls and royal menageries, these birds revitalize your map’s wetlands.

[size=4]What's a Shorebird?[/size]
"Shorebirds" belong to a wide array of coastal and wetland families, found on and around oceans, along coastlines, estuaries, inland marshes and riverbanks. Equipped with specialized bills—ranging from long, curved mud-probes to massive fish-scooping pouches—they are uniquely adapted to harvest the rich ecosystems where land meets water. Many of these birds are epic migrators, travelling thousands of miles and braving climate extremes to breed and raise young.

[size=4]The Avian Catalog[/size]
This mod introduces eight unique bird species, in two rough groups:

[b]The Waders and Swimmers (Water Seeking AI):[/b][/color]

[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Cormorant:[/b][/i] Heavy, webbed-foot diving birds. Famous for their signature low-profile "submarine" silhouette when hunting in rivers and oceans.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Egret:[/b][/i] Elegant, long-legged waders that stand frozen along muddy banks, waiting to spear prey. Their prized 'breeding plume' feathers are highly valued for high-society apparel accessories.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Ibis:[/b][/i] Highly prized ceremonial birds that probe deep into wetland mud in search of food. They are considered a massive status symbol and are restricted to exotic trade networks.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Pelican:[/b][/i] Large, buoyant, aquatic birds. Known for their large throat pouch and their love of resting on docks and piers. They often 'beg' fishermen to get free meals, though have never been domesticated.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Spoonbill:[/b][/i] Visually stunning waders that swing their unique bills side-to-side through shallow water to filter out nutrition. A highly valued, exotic luxury pet.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[b]The Beach Combers (Wild Fauna AI):[/b][/color]

[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Sandpiper:[/b][/i] Frantic, miniature 'peeps' that run rapidly along the sand chasing the wave line, searching among the sand for buried invertebrates. They have a very wide range of climates due to their equatorial to polar migrations for breeding.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Plover:[/b][/i] The inland kin of the sandpiper. While they share a similar tiny silhouette, they tend to stay higher up on dry gravel flats, fields, and forests away from the crushing waves.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Seagull:[/b][/i] Opportunistic coastal scavengers. They can survive on open water although they tend to prefer staying near dry land, often near human habitations where they scavenge among scraps and detritus for easy food.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/fVfublL.png[/img]

[size=4]Features[/size]
[/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Reworked Bird Leather:[/b][/i] Birdskin has been patched to accurately reflect the luxury use of feathers. No longer a junk textile, it serves as a high-value material needed to stitch together elite tribal wear and prestigious court ornaments.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Sacred Ibis Mummy:[/b][/i] Perform a ceremonial mummification ritual at a sculpting bench to preserve an ibis carcass in pristine linen and sacred resins. When placed in crypts or near sarcophagi this solemn monument boosts room beauty and accelerates psyfocus gain for morbid-focus colonists. Paintable to match your tomb-chamber aesthetic.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]Feathered Tribal Headdress, War Mask & Aigrette Hair Pin:[/b][/i] Early-game apparel geared towards tribal playthroughs, or simply to bring a unique look to your Royal court. Give your colonists, warriors, and chieftains unique beautiful feathered headwear that affects social impact or warrior pain shock threshold. All are fully dyable.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][i][b]The Feather Banner:[/b][/i] A majestic ceremonial standard that satisfies noble decoration demands. Banner poles like these have been used by many cultures to showcase an elegant, shimmering display of colorful feathers collected from valuable and important birds. Paintable to match your throne room aesthetic.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=4]Mod Notes[/size]
NOT CE COMPATIBLE. I hate writing code and have asked on the CE discord for patches to my bird mods but nobody ever gets back to me. I'll update this if it happens.

Should be compatible with pretty much anything else (let me know any issues so I can do my best to fix). [b]Includes support for most popular biome mods.[/b] Please contact me if you would like me to add yours.
[i]There is one exception to this: My seagulls will not spawn in any of the "Biomes! Islands" islands or coasts; That author already has seagulls native to those biomes. The rest of my birds will spawn in them just fine.[/i]

I highly recommend something like Camera+ to enjoy the colors and sounds of these animals.
[/color]

Download, extract, place into you Mods folder in your Rimworld install directory[/color]

nodes.name: StormProof
nodes.summary: Defend your grid from everything the Rim throws at it: solar flares, lightning, power surges, and EMP.
nodes.description:
SOLAR SHIELD
A field generator that idles at 100W - until a solar flare hits, when it draws a massive 2,500W continuously to keep your colony's electronics alive through the whole event. Keep your batteries charged: if the grid runs dry mid-flare, the shield fails and everything goes dark until the flare passes.

STORM SPIRE
A grounded spire that attracts lightning strikes within its radius, keeping fires away from your base. The spire cannot burn and snuffs out any flames a caught strike sparks around it. Connect it to your power grid and it becomes a harvester: each caught strike dumps up to 1,500 Wd into your batteries - but carries a 5% chance of overloading the grid and triggering a "Zzzt!" power surge. Late-game perfect grounding research eliminates the surge risk entirely.

STORM CAPACITOR BANK
A lightning-only battery. Only spire-caught strikes can fill it, but it never self-discharges and "Zzzt!" surges can't touch it. Automatically discharges up to 2,000W when grid production falls short.

SURGE PROTECTOR
Absorbs one "Zzzt!" short circuit event, then needs a day to recharge (and takes some internal damage). Pairs dangerously well with a grid-connected storm spire.

WEATHER FORECASTER
A barometric console that shows how long the current weather will hold, announces incoming thunderstorms, and warns you an hour before the weather breaks.

STATIC DISCHARGE PYLON
Runs exclusively on bottled lightning: every shock drains 50 Wd from a storm capacitor bank on its power net to stun and burn hostile raiders and mechanoids in a small radius. No capacitor charge, no zap.

FALLOUT SCRUBBER
Filters airborne toxins out of an enclosed room - pawns and animals inside slowly shed toxic buildup, faster than fallout adds it.

STORM CALLER
Late-game ionospheric agitator that summons a rainy thunderstorm on demand: lightning for your spires, rain for your wildfires. Five-day recharge.

EMP DAMPENER
Powered buildings near the dampener shrug off EMP stuns - turrets keep firing through EMP mortar barrages.

ARMORED CONDUIT
A fireproof, high-durability conduit for hardened bases.

STORM VANE
A decorative copper weather vane. It doesn't do anything. It looks great.

nodes.name: Deity Grammar Fix
nodes.summary: Fixes the r_deityType grammar error during ideology and world generation by supplying the missing memeConceptDef grammar bridge. Uses a lightweight, language-independent Harmony patch.
nodes.description:
Have you ever encountered a Grammar unresolvable error involving r_deityType during world generation, followed by Failed to resolve text. Trying again with English? This mod adds a lightweight, language-independent Harmony Prefix that supplies the missing grammar bridge when deity types are generated, preventing the error and stopping RimWorld from retrying that specific text generation using English grammar.
[line]
[b]🌸 General Description[/b]
This mod implements a lightweight C# fix using Harmony to add the missing memeConceptDef grammar bridge directly to deity-type generation requests when the symbol is unavailable. It was created after reproducing the problem in Spanish (Latin), but the patch itself is not tied to a specific language and can correct the same grammar mismatch in any language where it occurs. The fix only runs when RimWorld is resolving r_deityType, and it does not replace an existing valid memeConceptDef rule.
[line]
[b]✨ Key Features[/b]
[list]
[*][color=#00ff00]✔[/color] Prevents the Grammar unresolvable. Root 'r_deityType' error caused by a missing memeConceptDef rule.[/*]
[*][color=#00ff00]✔[/color] Prevents RimWorld from retrying the affected deity-type text generation using English grammar.[/*]
[*][color=#00ff00]✔[/color] Uses a narrowly targeted Harmony Prefix.[/*]
[*][color=#00ff00]✔[/color] Language-independent and able to correct the same mismatch in other languages.[/*]
[*][color=#00ff00]✔[/color] Does not replace an existing valid grammar rule.[/*]
[*][color=#00ff00]✔[/color] Designed to be compatible with ongoing saves.[/*]
[/list][line]
[b]🛠️ Technical Details and Compatibility[/b]
This mod modifies the internal C# logic using Harmony.
[list]
[*][b]Requirements:[/b] Harmony must be installed for this to work. The affected deity-generation system belongs to the Ideology DLC, so this fix is only relevant when Ideology is active.[/*]
[*][b]Load Order:[/b] Place this mod after Harmony, Core, and the DLCs. Generally, no special placement relative to other mods should be necessary.[/*]
[*][b]Targeted Method:[/b] RimWorld.NameGenerator:GenerateName.
Targeted Grammar Root: r_deityType.
Added Grammar Bridge: memeConceptDef->[memeConcept]. [/*]
[*][color=#ffff00]⚠[/color] This mod targets RimWorld 1.6. While it may work on older versions, they are outside the scope of testing and support.[/*]
[/list][line]
[b]📥 Installation[/b]

[list=1]
[*]Download the file.[/*]
[*]Extract the folder into your RimWorld [b]Mods [/b]directory.[/*]
[*]Activate the mod in your in-game Mod Manager or [b]RimSort[/b].[/*]
[*]Make sure it loads after all the DLCs[i].[/i][/*]
[/list][line]
[b]❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)[/b]

[b]1. Does this mod only work with Spanish (Latin)?[/b]
No. The patch is language-independent and runs for any language when RimWorld generates an r_deityType result. However, it only fixes the specific situation where memeConceptDef is missing but memeConcept is available. Spanish (Latin) is currently the language in which the issue was reproduced and tested.
[b]2. Does this mod require the Ideology DLC?[/b]
The mod can load without Ideology, but it will have nothing relevant to fix because deity and ideology generation belong to that DLC. Harmony is the only required framework dependency.
[b]3. Does this mod change deity names or add custom deity types?[/b]
No. It does not add custom names, concepts, or deity types. It only allows RimWorld's existing grammar rules to resolve the missing symbol correctly.
[b]4. Does it work on saved games?[/b]
Yes! This fix is intended to be safe to add to an ongoing playthrough. It does not store any custom save data and only affects deity-type grammar requests generated while the mod is active.
[b]5. Does this mod affect performance?[/b]
No noticeable impact. The Prefix only checks whether a name-generation request is using the r_deityType
grammar root and adds one missing rule when necessary.
[b]6. Is it worth using this mod if I haven't seen any errors yet?
[/b] Yes, especially if you use Ideology in Spanish (Latin) or another language affected by the same grammar mismatch. The error is intermittent and may not appear during every world generation.
[b]7. Do you accept requests for fixing bugs in other mods?
[/b] Unfortunately, no. I am currently focusing on resolving the specific red errors within my own mod list. I only work on fixes for mods that I am actively using and testing in my own game as I encounter issues.
[b]8. What kind of testing has been performed?[/b]
In-game testing was performed in Spanish (Latin) across three separate game launches and more than ten world-generation attempts. The error previously appeared intermittently after the planet and its factions were generated, and it did not reappear while the runtime fix was active.
[b]9. Are there other grammar bugs or localization incompatibilities in RimWorld?[/b]
I have not audited the complete grammar and localization system, so I cannot confirm whether this is the only issue. This patch specifically targets the missing memeConceptDef rule reported by the r_deityType error.
[b]10. Does this mod work on RimWorld 1.5 or earlier?[/b]
It’s possible. This patch was developed and tested for version 1.6. Earlier versions might also work if the targeted method has the same signature. I do not offer technical support or perform compatibility testing for versions prior to 1.6. If you still want to try it, go to: 
Mods\DeityGrammarFix\About\About.xml
Open the file with a text editor, change the supported game version from 1.6 to your version of RimWorld, save the file, and then test it at your own risk. Changing About.xml only removes the unsupported-version warning and does not guarantee compatibility.
[b]11. Are more updates planned for this mod?[/b]
Currently, this patch is focused on the r_deityType grammar issue. However, I may release updates if I discover other closely related grammar bugs or if a RimWorld update changes or officially fixes the affected code .
[b]12. Has this bug been reported to the RimWorld developers? [/b]
Yes. The issue has been reported to the RimWorld developers together with the console error and relevant stack trace. If the bug is officially fixed in a future game update, this standalone patch may no longer be necessary.
[b]13. Do you plan to publish more mods?[/b]
Yes. I currently have more fixes in the testing phase, including patches related to Humanoid Alien Races compatibility and more. Keep an eye on my Nexus profile.
[b]14. Does the source script have comments in Spanish?[/b]
Yes. My native language is Spanish, so if you ever decompile the DLL, you will find my developer comments written in Spanish.
[b]15. What should I do if RimWorld is updated?
[/b] In most cases, you can keep this fix active. Since it uses a dynamic Harmony patch, it is designed to remain compatible unless the developers significantly rename or rewrite the targeted method. If a game update causes the error to return, creates a new error, or officially fixes the original bug, please let me know so I can update or retire this patch.
[b]16. Can I ask you questions about the mod, Harmony, or other related topics?[/b]
Yes. Don't hesitate—just ask! I will respond as soon as possible.
[b]17. Is this mod on Steam?[/b]
It’s currently not on Steam Workshop. However, you are free to upload this mod there.

My goal was to provide a reliable experience for everyone. If this fix helped you, do not forget to leave your 👍 endorsement on Nexus. It helps other players find this fix.[/i] ❤❤❤[/quote]

nodes.description:
[size=5]How To Use[/size]
This mod might bug out your stoves if you load it mid-game while you have bulk recipe bills present. The way to avoid bugs is to either:
1: After you load a save and see the bug, save the game again, then load the new save.
2: Make sure you have no bulk recipe bills in any of your stoves in the save you're loading.


Simple mod to remove all bulk recipes from cooking in the game. This mod can be seen as a way to challenge yourself when it comes to organisation and time management. But I mainly made this mod to avoid accidentally encountering a bug in this game of kitchens not producing 1-3 meals because they don't have enough ingredients to fulfill the bill for a bulk x4 meals.

Currently only works on meals/pemmican recipes. Not functioning for drugs for some reason.


I thought of the idea to make this mod after I created my [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3754430739]Realistic Pemmican [/url]mod. So it's just because first when I started playing this game I was unaware that bulk x4 recipes were faster than individual recipes so I just played making meal 1 at a time and I thought the only way to increase meals production rate was just creating more stoves or creating longer shifts for the cooks to make meals throughout the day. Then I ran into the bug that sometimes when you only have enough ingredients to make 1, 2 or 3 meals but the stove has the order to produce bulk x4 meals then the cook won't make anything because there's not enough ingredients to make 4.

Just the way that bulk orders for stove bills was designed and executed in this game wasn't done properly so I thought of the simplest solution being to just disable them outright. This mod effects only meals and pemmican bulk orders. Maybe some mods depending on the load order and if they have the number "4" in the name of the stove's bill tab.

Also I recommend [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3524727262]Workbench Connect [/url]to use with this mod or just in general that lets you connect multiple stoves in a link kind of like how you can link shelves to store the same stuff. I just found it dumb this wasn't in the base game already.

Just a few simple functions and features are missing in the base game that should already be inside.

nodes.name: Realistic Pemmican
nodes.summary: Instead of 18 units of pemmican being the equivalent of 1 meal, now 1.125 units of pemmican is equivalent to 1 meal. This means no more stupid numbers like needing 180 units of pemmican to feed people as much as 10 meals or carrying 1000s
nodes.description:
[size=5]What this mod does:[/size]

1: Everything in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2761817611]Practical Pemmican[/url]. So instead of 18 units of pemmican being the equivalent of 1 meal, now 1.125 units of pemmican is equivalent to 1 meal. This means no more stupid numbers like needing 180 units of pemmican to feed people as much as 10 meals or carrying 1000s of units of pemmican just to send a caravan for several days. Obviously because the nutritional value has been multiplied by 16, the units of output for the same amount of ingredients has been divided by 16 also, the weight and market value has been multiplied by 16. So pretty much practically pemmican is the same, the big difference is that now it's not divided into so many stupid pieces.

2: Changes the basic pemmican recipes to be 100% meat.

3: Adds another x1 and bulk x4 recipe for pemmican with 90% meat.


[size=5]Why:[/size]

This mod is a combination of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3618195343]Practical Pemmican 1.6 [/url]/ [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2761817611]Practical Pemmican [/url]with modified ingredient requirements I thought of when I was searching for a carnivorous pemmican recipe mod online.

I didn't particularly think any pre-existing mod was perfect so I combined and modified them for my personal use. I hope you enjoy it also.

All this does is the same things as the original "Practical Pemmican" mod with the addition of modified ingredients and a new 2nd pemmican recipe.

The reason I made this mod is because I particularly hated how in this game pemmican was only 50% meat and there was no 90% or 100% meat pemmican options.

I recommend you use [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2950042909][HB] Pemmican 2.0 Reskin[/url] alongside this to improve the looks for Pemmican also, turn them in to stacks of canned meat.

[line]
[heading]Origin[/heading]
Have you ever wondered—what if your colony is being live-streamed in another dimension? Countless viewers are glued to their screens, watching your every decision: they spam “danmaku shield” when a raid hits, mock your pawns when they break, and flood the chat with “666” when research completes…
[b]RimTuber[/b] adds an immersive live-stream danmaku window to your game, turning your colony into a real streaming channel!
[line]
[heading]Core Features[/heading]
Danmaku System
[list]
[*][b]Real-time danmaku window[/b]: draggable, resizable, with adjustable opacity. When minimized, only the title and the latest danmaku are shown—never blocking your view.[/*]
[*][b]Smart danmaku content[/b]: messages dynamically reflect game events—tense spam during raids, sarcastic roasts during mental breaks, cheers and applause during celebrations.[/*]
[*][b]Viewer personality system[/b]: each viewer has a unique personality—simp, troll, newbie, memelord, tactics nerd, jinxer, organ-trader fan, and 30+ archetypes, each with a distinct speaking style.[/*]
[*][b]Viewer ranks[/b]: viewers can level up to Captain, Admiral, or Governor! Higher ranks chat more frequently and have increased gift probabilities.[/*]
[*][b]Streamer chat[/b]: you can also join the danmaku! Set your streamer name, type messages in the chat box, and viewers will give AI-generated replies based on what you say.[/*]

[/list]AI Danmaku (Highly Recommended)
[list]
[*][b]Multi-AI support[/b]: works with Gemini / OpenAI / DeepSeek / Grok / GLM / OpenRouter / SiliconFlow / Player2. No API key? No problem—local template mode runs just fine![/*]
[*][b]Context awareness[/b]: the AI reads real in-game data—current weather, colonist status, letters, prisoner count, research progress—to generate relevant danmaku.[/*]
[*][b]Trending memes[/b]: the AI proactively gathers and uses the hottest internet slang and memes, making the chat feel like a genuine modern livestream.[/*]
[*][b]Batch generation[/b]: each AI call produces 2–3 danmaku from different viewers, with a 10-second cooldown—saving tokens while keeping the flow natural.[/*]
[*][b]RimTalk integration[/b]: when used with RimTalk and its memory extension, common-sense knowledge is injected to enrich danmaku context.[/*]

[list]
